data.title: RDGA Registrar Concentration Anomaly
data.description: Detects anomalous concentration of new domain registrations at a single registrar that share lexical similarity patterns and nameserver infrastructure, indicating RDGA-driven bulk registration campaigns. Threat actors frequently exploit registrars with weak abuse controls, automated APIs, or low-cost bulk pricing to register large volumes of algorithmically generated domains. This rule correlates three signals: high registration volume at a single registrar, lexical similarity among the registered domain names (e.g., consonant-vowel patterns, character n-gram overlap, or string edit distance clustering), and shared nameserver delegation. The combination of these factors distinguishes RDGA activity from legitimate bulk registration by portfolio investors or brand protection services. Supports TP-0041 Phase 2 detection of registrar abuse for RDGA infrastructure provisioning.

detection.condition: selection and aggregation and lexical_similarity and nameserver_overlap

enrichment_required.source: DNS analytics enrichment (shared nameserver ratio calculation)

falsepositives: Domain portfolio investors acquiring thematically similar domain names in bulk
Brand protection services registering typosquatting variants defensively
New gTLD land-rush registrations with common keyword patterns
